2. Whether this Court has territorial jurisdiction to try and entertain the suit for partition qua the property situated in village Muneerpur, District Sonipat, Haryana?
OPD 43.

This issue has been framed in view of the objection taken by the defendants to the effect that as some of the properties are situated in Haryana and some of them are situated in CSDJ13969/2016 Satbir Singh & Anr. vs. Bihari Lal & Ors. 14 of 19 Delhi, the Delhi Courts have no territorial jurisdiction qua the properties situated in Haryana.

entities.text: CSDJ13969/2016 Satbir Singh & Anr. vs. Bihari Lal & Ors. 14 of 19
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 44. However, as per Section 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), in case of properties situated in different jurisdictions, any court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction any portion of the property is situated, has the jurisdiction to try the suit with respect to all the properties.

45. As some of the the suit properties are situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Delhi Court,
in terms of the provisions of Section 17 CPC, this court has territorial jurisdiction to entertain and try this suit.
46. Issue no.2 is accordingly decided against the defendants.
4. Whether the suit is without any cause of action ?
OPD 47.

As per the defendants, the suit is without any cause of action as the defendant no.1's marriage with the plaintiff no.2 stand dissolved in 1963 in a family panchayat and in lieu of said dissolution,
the plaintiff no.2 was duly compensated and out of the said compensation, both the plaintiffs have purchased sufficient properties and accordingly are debarred from asking for a share in the joint HUF properties.
48.

However, the law is very well settled that with respect to the marriages governed by the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, no such divorce can be granted by a family panchayat as held CSDJ13969/2016 Satbir Singh & Anr. vs. Bihari Lal & Ors. 15 of 19 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of 'Yamanaji H. Jadav vs. Nirmla(2002) 2 SCC 637 and as recent as on 28.11.2025 by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the matter of 'Sushma vs. Ratandeep' MAT. APPL.(F.C.) 281/2024 and CM APPL. No.
48706/2024.
49.

18. Hence, the present suit seeking the following relief(s):-
a. A decree for partition of all the suit properties by metes and bounds between the plaintiffs and the defendants herein defining and determining the rightful share /its value in favour of the plaintiffs in the said suit properties.
b. A decree for declaration that the plaintiffs are the owners of their rightful share in the suit properties therein in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants.
d. A decree for injunction against the defendants restraining them from undertaking any further construction/modification/alteration within the suit premises in violation of the rules/notifications/ directions etc. of the DDA and from leasing/
mortgaging/renting/alienating the suit properties in any form whatsoever which is prejudicial to the interest of the plaintiffs and their share in the suit property.
They have also taken objection qua the under-valuation of the suit properties.
24. It is alleged that the marriage between the plaintiff no.2 and defendants no.1 stands dissolved in 1963 in a family panchayat and the plaintiff no.2 was suitably compensated for the maintenance of herself as well as plaintiff no.1 at the time of dissolution of marriage and out of the said compensation, the plaintiffs have purchased the properties for their own use, and, as such, the plaintiffs cannot maintain the present suit, as per the defendants.
25.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
20. As per them, this court is having no territorial jurisdiction with respect to the properties situated in the State of Haryana as the said properties cannot be clubbed with the properties situated in Delhi.
The PW-1 was extensively cross-
41. However, the defendants have not led even an a single piece of evidence to challenge the valuation of the suit properties, as adopted by the plaintiff in the plaint, by leading any independent evidence to disprove the said evidence and even from the cross-examination of PW1, nothing adverse in this respect has come on record.
This issue has been framed in view of the objection taken by the defendants to the effect that as some of the properties are situated in Haryana and some of them are situated in CSDJ13969/2016 Satbir Singh & Anr. vs. Bihari Lal & Ors. 14 of 19 Delhi, the Delhi Courts have no territorial jurisdiction qua the properties situated in Haryana.
44. However, as per Section 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), in case of properties situated in different jurisdictions, any court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction any portion of the property is situated, has the jurisdiction to try the suit with respect to all the properties.
As per the defendants, the suit is without any cause of action as the defendant no.1's marriage with the plaintiff no.2 stand dissolved in 1963 in a family panchayat and in lieu of said dissolution,
the plaintiff no.2 was duly compensated and out of the said compensation, both the plaintiffs have purchased sufficient properties and accordingly are debarred from asking for a share in the joint HUF properties.
48.
However, the law is very well settled that with respect to the marriages governed by the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, no such divorce can be granted by a family panchayat as held CSDJ13969/2016 Satbir Singh & Anr. vs. Bihari Lal & Ors. 15 of 19 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of 'Yamanaji H. Jadav vs. Nirmla(2002) 2 SCC 637 and as recent as on 28.11.2025 by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the matter of 'Sushma vs. Ratandeep' MAT. APPL.(F.C.) 281/2024 and CM APPL. No.
48706/2024.
49.
In these circumstances, the said ground of divorce between the plaintiff no.2 and defendant no.1 being not tenable, the plaitniff no.1 being the son and the plaitniff no.2 being the wife of deceased-defendant no.1, they have every right to claim partition in the properties inherited by defendant no.1 from his forefathers and that too even during his lifetime as the said properties were part of joint family properties.
50.
As the defendants are enjoying the said properties, the plaintiffs are held entitled to seek share in the said properties also.
In view of the fact that the defendants have failed to prove any of their submissions by virtue of evidence, whereas, the plaintiffs have been able to prove the khasra girdawari/ jamabandi of the suit properties in the name of defendant no.1, the plaintiffs being son and wife of defendant no.1, are held as entitled to a decree of partition qua the suit properties.
